CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding - elevated blood sugar

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
55-year-old male with past medical history of anxiety and epilepsy presents following emergency room visit for significantly elevated blood glucose. Patient was treated in the ER for hyperglycemia. Patient attributes the acute elevation to recent travel and entertainment with multiple visitors over the past couple of weeks, during which he was not monitoring sugar intake and experienced increased stress and strain. Patient reports feeling well since the ER visit. Prior hemoglobin A1C values were borderline, but are now elevated. Patient was started on metformin in the emergency room. Regarding anxiety, patient reports having had moments of anxiety but notes that his symptoms have improved as the weekend approaches and feels things are under control. Regarding epilepsy, patient denies any seizures in several months, with the last episode being minor.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, or dizziness. Denies recent fever or chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Anxiety
2. Epilepsy

MEDICATIONS
1. Metformin 500 mg twice daily
2. Keppra

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient has been traveling with multiple visitors over the past couple of weeks.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Within normal limits
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm
Extremities: Trace pitting edema to lower extremities

RESULTS
Blood Glucose: 162 mg/dL (2 hours post-prandial)
Hemoglobin A1C: 8.0% (previously approximately 6%)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Newly Diagnosed Diabetes Mellitus - Continue Metformin 500 mg twice daily with plan to increase over time. Order hemoglobin A1C for future monitoring. Trace pitting edema likely secondary to IV fluid administration in emergency room.
2. Anxiety - Patient open to trying new medication to help manage symptoms, particularly with potential seasonal challenges approaching.
3. Epilepsy - Continue Keppra. Patient to follow up with neurologist as scheduled.
